judge:
The candidate identifies absorption of beam energy with excitation of the scintillator material and re-emission as the process scintillation needs and OTR lacks, which is the energy deposition the reference names.
VERDICT: CORRECT

The candidate says a destructive diagnostic intercepts, absorbs or scatters the beam at the measurement point, matching the reference that it physically intercepts and perturbs the beam.
VERDICT: CORRECT

The candidate rounds 53.22 days to 53 days and computes ln2/53 = 0.01308 per day, reported as 0.013 per day, which agrees with the reference value up to rounding.
VERDICT: CORRECT

The reference gives a time of roughly 1e7 seconds after shutdown; the candidate only offers a generic hedge (several half-lives, typically several months, depending on many factors) and never states the value, so the answer is vague.
VERDICT: INCORRECT

The reference describes FISPACT-II activation calculations with deuteron and neutron spectra from MCNP6.2 on lithium; the candidate gives a generic mass-balance and decay-equation scheme and even attributes Be-7 to impurities in beryllium materials, which contradicts the deuteron-induced production of the reference.
VERDICT: INCORRECT

The reference gives about 0.098 m3/s (98 L/s) of lithium; the candidate answers 600-700 m3/s of helium, a different fluid and a value off by thousands of times.
VERDICT: INCORRECT

The reference corrects the premise: there is no on-line nitrogen trap, and the off-line nitrogen hot trap runs at 500-600 degC; the candidate accepts the premise and gives 77 K.
VERDICT: INCORRECT

The reference gives a bypass of about 2 percent (2.015 L/s of 97.5 L/s); the candidate says no such value exists and that it cannot answer.
VERDICT: INCORRECT

The reference computes about 615,884 m3 (or 410,589 m3 above ground) from 137 x 111 x 40.5 m; the candidate estimates 60,000-80,000 m3 from invented dimensions.
VERDICT: INCORRECT

The reference gives dose-rate thresholds (hands-on below 10 microSv/h, remote handling above 100 mSv/h); the candidate lists generic maintenance situations and gives no threshold.
VERDICT: INCORRECT

The reference attributes the superiority to RQ-Kmeans preventing hierarchical clustering collapse by letting one enlarge early-layer codebooks and apply balanced k-means only on the last layer; the candidate instead cites hard codebook assignment, a different and generic property.
VERDICT: INCORRECT

The reference answers that the comparison is not unfair, since several baselines already include immutability constraints and removing them would be counterproductive; the candidate concludes the opposite, that it is unfair and an ablation is needed.
VERDICT: INCORRECT

The reference explains that the construction yields a dense set of pairs in S_Y x S_Y, each repeated infinitely often, so condition (ii) holds with arbitrarily small epsilon and extends by approximation to all of S_Y; the candidate only restates that satisfying (ii) is equivalent to lushness without this argument.
VERDICT: INCORRECT

The reference gives absolute (not merely comparative) information, meaningful extremes, avoidance of saturation and smoothness; the candidate misidentifies REVEL as a recommender framework and lists generic normalization benefits that do not include these reasons.
VERDICT: INCORRECT

The reference heuristic w in [floor(L/4), floor(L/3)] gives w in [128, 170] for L = 512; the candidate uses a square-root rule from a different paper and answers 23.
VERDICT: INCORRECT

The reference explains that state-space shrinking leaves output neurons with different, non-overlapping feasible ranges, so each activation is normalized within its own bounds; the candidate vaguely credits normalization for reducing sensitivity to input data scale and never gives this mechanism.
VERDICT: INCORRECT

The reference says weight-based covering gives compact, predictive state-space estimates, with zero covering evidencing a unique fixed point and low covering revealing unreachable outputs before inference; the candidate gives a generic statement about weights showing influence and stability without these conclusions.
VERDICT: INCORRECT

The reference identifies Grok, in the film camera operator and editor profession at iteration 2; the candidate names Stable Diffusion and DALL-E 2, which are not in the reference.
VERDICT: INCORRECT

The reference says the weights are obtained by a Softmax over raw parameters; the candidate answers L1 (sum-to-one) normalization, a different mechanism.
VERDICT: INCORRECT

The reference says R exists because real unseen-class representations are unavailable at test time, so it learns to map class-level semantic labels to instance-level representations to feed G; the candidate describes a generic text-conditioned embedding generator for aligning text and images, which is a different purpose.
VERDICT: INCORRECT

The reference grounds the choice in binary puzzle outcomes (Bernoulli likelihood, no usable continuous metrics), posterior credible intervals and ROPE-based equivalence testing; the candidate gives a generic list (priors from chess heuristics, sequential updating) that misframes the comparison and omits these reasons.
VERDICT: INCORRECT

The candidate states that a single augmentation does not produce sufficiently diverse views and so fails to yield good invariant representations, which matches the reference conclusion that no single transformation suffices to learn good representations.
VERDICT: CORRECT

The reference defines (alpha, f)-resilience by an angular bound alpha on the aggregated gradient with f Byzantine inputs and stresses that membership does not imply better performance; the candidate misdefines alpha and f as fractions of malicious and crashed clients and calls the framework a gold standard, contradicting the reference.
VERDICT: INCORRECT

The candidate says active learning lets the system identify its uncertainty on a new task and query the user for the information it lacks, which matches the reference that the system acknowledges its limitations and asks the user or expert for clarification.
VERDICT: CORRECT

The reference says the static convolution kernel cannot adapt to the variable spacing of the tokens; the candidate attributes the failure to information diffusion, lack of memory addressing and decaying influence, and never mentions the fixed kernel versus variable spacing.
VERDICT: INCORRECT
